title: On Linux the desktop app keeps Chromium's cookie key in the basic store, so no keyring dialog blocks the first window; macOS and Windows keep their OS store
expect: S1: passwordStoreSwitch returns 'basic' for platform linux with no --password-store on the command line.
S1: it returns null for darwin and win32.
S1: it returns null on linux when the launch already names --password-store.
S1: main.js applies it before app.whenReady and after refuseDebugSwitches; debugGuardFirst(main.js) is still true.
evidence: Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME auto-login, 0.4.0/0.5.0: 'Choose password for new keyring' at first launch, blank window (test/desktop-0-5-0-winlinux-smoke, tasks/evidence/desktop-onboard/2026-10-11-winlinux-smoke/linux/L01, L21, L02)
fence: A Linux launch never asks the Secret Service for Chromium's cookie key unless the person names a store

tests: Linux keeps the cookie key in the basic store
macOS and Windows keep their own OS store
a store the person names on the command line wins
main.js sets the store before app.whenReady
